post.caption:
Three algorithms. One maze. Which finds the best route?

In this maze, Greedy checks the fewest squares ({greedy.expanded}) but takes a {greedy.extra}-step detour: its route is {greedy.path} steps instead of {optimal}. BFS spreads out in all directions and finds the shortest route after checking {bfs.expanded} squares. A* finds an equally short route after checking only {astar.expanded}.

A*'s trick: steps taken so far, plus an estimate of the distance left that never overshoots, so it never settles for a longer route.

(Squares checked is a count of the work, not a stopwatch: real running time also depends on the cost of each step.)

Search smart, not everywhere.
